entry.title: Toolchain 5.0 lands with breaking schema changes and plugin marketplace preview
entry.summary: Toolchain shipped major release v5.0.0 on 2025-03-12, introducing a breaking change to the config schema and reducing cold-start time by roughly 40%. It was quickly followed by v5.0.1 on 2025-03-14, which fixed a high-severity security issue (CVE-2025-99887) in the plugin loader. A preview of the new plugin marketplace also went live during the window.
entry.content:
Toolchain shipped major release v5.0.0 on 2025-03-12, introducing a breaking change to the config schema and reducing cold-start time by roughly 40%. It was quickly followed by v5.0.1 on 2025-03-14, which fixed a high-severity security issue (CVE-2025-99887) in the plugin loader. A preview of the new plugin marketplace also went live during the window.

Releases​

  • v5.0.0 was released on 2025-03-12. It introduces a breaking change to the config schema (old plugins list becomes a plugins: map) and cuts cold-start time by about 40%. Migration instructions are in the release notes. See GitHub release.
  • v5.0.1 was released on 2025-03-14 to patch the plugin-loader vulnerability; upgrading is strongly recommended. See GitHub release.
  • v4.3.2 was released on 2025-03-10 as a patch for the last 4.x line, fixing a rare infinite retry loop in the build cache. See GitHub release.

Features​

  • A preview of the plugin marketplace was published on 2025-03-13. It lets teams browse, pin, and share internal plugins, and is disabled by default until a marketplace: config block is added. See docs preview.

Fixes and other​

  • The security fix in v5.0.1 addresses CVE-2025-99887, a path traversal in the plugin loader rated high severity (7.2 CVSS). Details are in the security advisory.
  • A new migration guide for upgrading from v4 to v5 was published on 2025-03-11, covering config changes and CLI flags that were removed. See migration guide.

Community​

  • The monthly newsletter (#42) was published on 2025-03-14, covering the plugin marketplace launch, a call for community plugin authors, and a 2025 roadmap Q&A. See newsletter.

Sources​

  • https://github.com/acme/toolchain/releases/tag/v5.0.0
  • https://github.com/acme/toolchain/releases/tag/v5.0.1
  • https://github.com/acme/toolchain/releases/tag/v4.3.2
  • https://toolchain.dev/docs/plugins-preview
  • https://toolchain.dev/docs/migration-5
  • https://github.com/acme/toolchain/security/advisories/GHSA-2025-99887
  • https://toolchain.dev/newsletter/2025-03

entry.title: Welcome
entry.summary: Docusaurus blogging features are powered by the blog plugin.
entry.content:
Docusaurus blogging features are powered by the blog plugin.

Here are a few tips you might find useful.

Simply add Markdown files (or folders) to the blog directory.

Regular blog authors can be added to authors.yml.

The blog post date can be extracted from filenames, such as:

  • 2019-05-30-welcome.md
  • 2019-05-30-welcome/index.md

A blog post folder can be convenient to co-locate blog post images:

The blog supports tags as well!

And if you don't want a blog: just delete this directory, and use blog: false in your Docusaurus config.

entry.title: MDX Blog Post
entry.summary: Blog posts support Docusaurus Markdown features, such as MDX.
entry.content:
Blog posts support Docusaurus Markdown features, such as MDX.

tip

Use the power of React to create interactive blog posts.

For example, use JSX to create an interactive button:

<button onClick={() => alert('button clicked!')}>Click me!</button>
